trajectory_summary: This is a short, procedurally smooth call: the customer arrived pre-warmed from a form-fill, cooperated through verify items with minimal resistance, and the rep adapted efficiently to a genuine edge case (new homeowner with no bill history) by substituting a live kWh reading and checking with a supervisor. The call never builds real emotional charge — there's no bill-pain moment, no objection cycling, and no cross-sell probing — it simply proceeds calmly to a booked appointment.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; observed outcome is a booked appointment with a firm day and time (March 27th at noon) and a stated location constraint, so this should be tagged 'booked,' not left ambiguous.

observed_outcome.quote: K. So I got you twenty seventh at noon.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific date (the 27th) and time (noon) are locked, and the appointment is for someone to come to the customer's house, making this an in-person booked outcome. No co-owner was identified since the customer confirmed he is the sole person on the title.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I can tell you what my kilowatt usage is right now.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No dollar-amount bill was ever captured — the customer is a brand-new homeowner with no bill history, and the rep accepted a live kWh usage snapshot as a substitute for the utility bill. This satisfies the technical design-data requirement but leaves the emotional bill-pain anchor completely unestablished; the rep never asked what the customer expects to pay or reflected the usage number as a cost hook.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Yes. And, like, Allstate. You know?
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked directly ('What's your interest in solar? Just saving money?') and the customer's response is transcribed ambiguously ('Yes. And, like, Allstate. You know?') — the transcription does not yield a clear, usable reason beyond the rep's own suggested 'saving money' framing, which the customer simply affirmed rather than articulated himself. Treating this as a captured reason would overstate what's actually on the record.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I can tell you what my kilowatt usage is right now.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer never gave a dollar bill amount and the rep never asked what the customer expects a typical bill to be or reflected the kWh number back as a hook — the whole call proceeds on usage data alone with zero emotional anchor to cost. This is the single biggest gap: the appointment gets booked but the closer inherits zero bill-pain leverage to open with.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses he's out of state at the time of the call, which the rep never explicitly reconciles until scheduling — it resurfaces at 05:42 when the rep asks if he's out of town all week, but the intervening logistics (is he home for the appointment window) were not locked down until late in the call.

key_moments.quote: I don't know. I just bought the house.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the moment the schema's bill-amount capture should happen, but the customer has no bill history, creating a genuine data gap rather than a stall.

key_moments.quote: I can tell you what my kilowatt usage is right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep accepts a live kWh reading as sufficient qualification data but never converts it into a forward-pulling hook — no follow-up like 'that's a solid number to build a design around' or tying it to potential savings once he's home. The number is filed, not leveraged.
